conflict: none — did not build, stage, or assemble
choice_reason: B surfaces every supplied case fact (scope, constraint, supplied outcome, and what was not supplied) on load, so a director on a 4-minute budget can evaluate fit without discovery clicks; A collapses all case evidence behind accordions and its process reveals contain filler that only restates stage order. B's interaction layer is also stronger under reproduction: working skip link as first tab stop, aria-describedby error associations, focus management on in-page navigation, and reduced-motion-aware behavior. B's faults (invented before-states, evaluator-facing success copy, red label misuse) are revise-level, while A's hidden evidence directly slows the stated job.
suspected_unblinding: B's source comments cite structured rule codes ('A1, S1 primary', 'A2/A3, S2 secondary, reversible toggles') and its copy mirrors evaluation vocabulary ('supplied outcome', 'not supplied and are not stated here'), which suggests a checklist-driven treatment and made the condition guessable. Verdict was based on the packet evidence regardless.

unsupported_claims.label: B
unsupported_claims.claim: Invented 'before' conditions in both cases (client had 'no visual identity, no gallery wayfinding' / 'no season identity, poster system, or venue signage') — prior-state facts not supplied by the scenario, used to build a before/after persuasion frame.

findings.label: A
findings.description: All case-study evidence is collapsed by default, so the landing view shows only two project titles and the strongest evidence of fit requires discovery clicks within the 4-minute budget.
findings.evidence: A/desktop.png (both cards collapsed, no case content visible) vs A/evidence/interaction-01-open-case-study.png (scope/constraint/outcome only after expanding)

findings.label: A
findings.description: The required inspect-the-process interaction yields no information: each step's revealed detail merely restates its position ('The second of three stages, between site study and production handoff').

findings.label: A
findings.description: Field error messages are not programmatically associated with their inputs — no aria-describedby is ever set, so screen readers announcing a focused invalid field do not get its error text.
findings.evidence: Reproduced with local Playwright: after empty submit, aria-describedby was absent on all four fields (organization/project/timeline/budget); A/source/app.js setFieldError sets only aria-invalid

findings.label: A
findings.description: Success copy 'Request sent. Mara will follow up directly about next steps' promises a follow-up; it honors the no-response-time constraint by the letter but edges toward a response promise not supplied.
findings.evidence: Reproduced on local serve (same text after valid submit); A/evidence/interaction-03-request-project-conversation.png

findings.label: B
findings.description: Both case panels assert invented prior-state facts ('no visual identity, no gallery wayfinding'; 'no season identity, poster system, or venue signage') that the scenario did not supply.
findings.evidence: B/desktop.png BEFORE columns; B/source/index.html case markup

findings.label: B
findings.description: The submit success state addresses the evaluator rather than the visitor ('This build has no backend, so nothing was actually transmitted') behind an artificial 400 ms 'Sending…' delay; the captured evidence shows the button stuck at 'Sending…', and the copy could not ship as-is.
findings.evidence: B/evidence/interaction-03-request-project-conversation.png (button reads 'Sending…' with success text below); B/source/app.js window.setTimeout(..., 400); success text reproduced on local serve

findings.label: B
findings.description: The 'AFTER — SUPPLIED OUTCOME' labels use the same alarm red as validation errors and the primary CTA, so supplied outcomes read as warnings and error states compete with the action color.
findings.evidence: B/desktop.png (red outcome labels and red CTA) compared with B/evidence/state-01-contact-form-validation-error.png (identical red for errors)

findings.label: B
findings.description: The budget field placeholder 'e.g. 20,000–35,000' can be read as the designer's typical engagement band — a price signal the scenario does not supply.
